> **New: vega Proxy. Cut your LLM bill in half.** > > Put vega in front of the LLM you already use (OpenAI or Anthropic SDK). It learns your decisions from your LLM, then makes the routine ones itself in about 50 ms and sends the rest through, unchanged. Two lines of code. 10,000 decisions a month free. > > ```python > client = OpenAI(base_url="https://…/proxy/v1", default_headers={"x-vega-key": "vg_…"}) > ``` > > **[Start free at platform.embedding.in →](https://platform.embedding.in)** · [Docs](https://platform.embedding.in/docs) · [embedding.in](https://embedding.in)

laya is free and open source. If it helps you, sponsor the work on GitHub.

**New in 0.5: laya reads images, audio and video, takes 73k tokens, says when it should not decide, and keeps learning.** All open source under Apache 2.0 (`pip install -U laya`). - **Text, images, audio and video.** `agent.predict(...)` with `image=`, `audio=` or `video=` gives the same typed answers as for text. - **73,728 tokens of context.** Whole contracts, threads and logs in one read. - **Abstain and unbound**, explained below. - **Physics, not text generation.** Each candidate answer is a valley; the input is a particle that rolls and settles in one. Deterministic, constant cost, nothing generated. - **Any LLM as the reader.** One small decision engine on top of a frozen reader, from 0.8B to 27B. - **Continuous learning.** `from laya import Learner`: it answers from day one and learns from every answer your team confirms, on your own machine, in seconds on a CPU with no fine-tuning. - **A teacher for what it is unsure of.** `laya.Escalator(learner, teacher)` sends only the records it abstains on, finds unbound or is not yet sure of to your teacher (a review queue, a rules engine, or a model you serve yourself with `laya.vllm_teacher`), serves that answer and learns from it, so the teacher is needed less and less. [Guide](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/docs/vegaml.md#a-teacher-for-what-it-is-unsure-of). ### How abstain and unbound work The input is placed as a particle in a small decision space where every candidate answer is a valley. Where the particle settles, and how deep, is the answer and its probability. - **`abstain`**: it declines to commit. The threshold is calibrated so that, among the answers it does give, the error rate stays under the configured risk (10% by default). - **`prediction_set`**: the conformal set, every option the answer could still be at `alpha` 0.10. One option means it is sure; two or more means the input really is ambiguous. - **`unbound`**: the particle settled far from every valley, so the input looks unlike anything it knows (likely off-distribution). It is reported on every answer but does not route on its own: measured, it also fired on 71% of normal banking77 rows, so it would have sent most good answers to review. - **`route`**: what to do with it, `auto` or `review`. Without labels, `review` when it abstains or the set holds more than one option. With labels (`agent.fit` / `agent.calibrate`), a band placed where precision holds at 95% on your rows decides. Gate on `route`, never on a confidence number. ### Benchmarks at a glance **Continuous learning.** 14 decision templates (31 questions), each starting from about 600 generated examples, then learning from confirmed answers; scored on 60 held-out rows per template. | | day one | after 40 confirmed answers | after 120 | |---|---|---|---| | laya, `laya.Learner` | 84.7% | 91.6% | **96.0%** | | Jev 1.14, confirmed answers written into its criteria | **89.5%** | 91.5% | 92.6% | Jev leads on day one (23 of 31 questions); they are level at 40; laya leads at 120 (12 wins, 7 losses, 12 ties). Jev cannot be taught, only prompted, and is a hosted API (364 ms a request from India). **What learning costs.** laya learns from 300 answers in 34 s on 8 CPU threads, with no GPU (0.72 s an answer, 6.4 GB of RAM; on a GPU 40 ms and 2 GB). Fine-tuning the classic encoder on the same 300 rows takes 89 s on a GPU with 9 GB and rewrites all 421M weights. **Learning from a stream, November 2026** (4B reader, held-out rows): | | laya | Jev 1.14 | |---|---|---| | banking77, 924 held out, after 4,928 rows | **87.5%**, ECE 0.028, 92.5% routed auto at 91.5% precision | 79.4% as shipped (ECE 0.078), 85.7% with examples | | typed-decisions, 2,000 decisions, after 1,200 rows | 73.7%, ECE **0.031** | 74.7%, ECE 0.047 (level) | **Across readers**, one byte-identical decision engine, 50,676 held-out records: 0.8B 76.5%, 4B 79.1%, 27B 81.1%, ECE 0.010 to 0.021. **Where it loses.** Zero-shot on generic public suites a large hosted model leads. As a prompt-injection gate on real traffic (ToxicChat, 1.8% attacks), Jev untaught catches 79.1% at 0.3% refused against 73.0% at 0.7% for a fitted head. The benchmarks further down are for the classic encoder checkpoints. Under the hood the new engine comes from [vegaml](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/vegaml), installed with laya. For the classic encoder, name it (`laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya")`) or pass `vegaml=False`. > **[Studio, from Embedding Space](https://studio.embedding.in)** builds the starting set for your questions and runs it for you. > **Cite this work.** M, N.; M, A. From Laya to Vega: Open Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities. *Preprints* **2026**, 2026110781. **Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine.** Typed decisions over 100+ languages in a single forward pass — 33 ms — trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD), with a router that picks the right checkpoint per request.

## Installation ```bash python -m pip install laya ``` With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), run `uv add laya` in a uv project or `uv pip install laya` in a virtual environment. Python 3.10 or newer. Optional extras: `laya[serve]` (HTTP server), `laya[mcp]` (MCP server), `laya[langchain]` (LangChain and LangGraph), `laya[llamaindex]` (LlamaIndex selectors), `laya[crewai]` (CrewAI routing), `laya[onnx]` (ONNX Runtime), `laya[fast]` (TileLang GPU fast path), `laya[structured]` (pydantic models in `decide`), `laya[vision]` (Pillow and torchvision, for `predict(image=...)` and `predict(video=...)`), `laya[audio]` (soundfile, to decode audio files). Step-by-step setup for each platform, CPU-only or GPU PyTorch builds, and troubleshooting are in [Installation details](#installation-details). For TypeScript / Node.js / browser, see [`laya-ts/`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/tree/main/laya-ts/). npm releases (`npm install laya-ts`) are published from this repository's `laya-ts-v*` release tags. **Long documents.** `laya-multilingual` reads up to 8,192 tokens with `max_len=8192`. Measured accuracy and time by document length, reproducible with [`research/scripts/bench_long_context.py`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/research/scripts/bench_long_context.py):

## Quickstart Since 0.5.0 `laya.Agent()` loads laya's new engine: a frozen 0.8B reader with a small physics engine on top, so every answer carries a conformal prediction set, an abstain flag, an out-of-distribution flag and a route decided without a threshold you had to guess at. Text, images, speech and 73k-token documents go through the same call. Python 3.10 or newer; details in [vega inside laya](#vega-inside-laya-agentvegamltrue). ```bash python -m pip install -U laya # 0.5.0 or newer: the new engine is the default ``` ```python import laya agent = laya.Agent() # the new engine with a 0.8B reader, the default since 0.5.0 # Switching the model underneath is one string. Every option keeps the same engine, questions and fields: # laya.Agent(vegaml="4b") # the Qwen3.5-4B reader from the same Hub repo # laya.Agent(vegaml="gemma-1b") # the gemma-3-1b-it reader, same repo # laya.Agent(vegaml="nandakishorm/vega-U") # any Hub repo id holding a vega-U checkpoint # laya.Agent(vegaml="./my-reader/") # a local dir from VegaAgent.attach(...), your own LLM ported in # laya.Agent(vegaml=True, backbone="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B") # name the reader weights explicitly, e.g. a mirror # Naming one of laya's own encoders loads it instead (or pass vegaml=False): # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya") # English, 33 ms on a T4 # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya-multilingual") # 100+ languages, up to 8,192 tokens with max_len=8192 # laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya-typed-decisions") # fine-tuned for the typed-decisions workflows state = "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan." questions = { "department": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which department should handle this?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors", "other": "everything else"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How urgent is this?", "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "blocking"]}, "churn_risk": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"}, } out = agent.predict(state, questions) ans = out["answers"]["department"] print(ans["choice"]) # billing print(ans["probabilities"]) # {"billing": 0.91, "technical": 0.04, "other": 0.05} print(ans["prediction_set"]) # ["billing"]: the options the answer could still be, at alpha 0.1 print(ans["abstain"]) # False: the engine is not refusing this one print(ans["unbound"]) # False: the state looks like something it has seen (reported, never routes) print(ans["route"]) # "auto"; "review" when the engine abstains or the set holds more than one print(out["answers"]["churn_risk"]["noul"]) # probability the answer is yes ``` The output keeps laya's shape (`choice`, `score`, `noul`, `probabilities`, `answer_confidence`) and adds vega's fields. Gate on `route`, not on a confidence number: it comes from the conformal set and the fitted band, which stay right on answers where the top probability does not. **Model switching.** Keep a laya encoder for short English text and let vega take the rest: ```python from laya.vega import Router router = Router(fast=laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya"), vega=agent) out = router.predict(state, questions) print(out["routing"]) # {"model": "fast", "reason": "short English text, no fitted head: the fast encoder is enough"} out = router.predict("मुझसे मार्च में दो बार शुल्क लिया गया, कृपया डुप्लिकेट राशि वापस करें।", questions) print(out["routing"]["model"]) # vega: non-English goes to the reader ``` The rule, in order: an image or audio goes to vega; text longer than the fast model's context goes to vega; non-English or non-Latin text goes to vega; a question with a fitted head goes to vega; everything else goes to the encoder. `model="vega"` or `model="fast"` forces one. **Images, speech, video, long documents.** The questions and the answer shape do not change with the input: ```python # text: up to 73,728 tokens in one pass; usage["truncated"] says if a state hit the limit agent.predict_long(seventy_page_contract, questions) # image: PIL image, path or HxWx3 array, any format Pillow opens; scaled to ~1 megapixel, no file-size cap # needs pip install 'laya[vision]' (Pillow and torchvision), as does video agent.predict(image="invoice.png", questions=questions) # audio: path or bytes (wav, flac, ogg, mp3; needs pip install 'laya[audio]') or a 1-D waveform with sampling_rate=; # any length, resampled to 16 kHz, transcribed in 30 s windows, transcript counts toward the 73,728 tokens agent.predict(audio=wave, questions=questions, sampling_rate=16000) # video: path or bytes, any container ffmpeg opens, any length and resolution (needs the ffmpeg binary); # speech is transcribed and decided as text, a silent clip is decided on 4 sampled frames as one image agent.predict(video="call.mp4", questions=questions) ``` **Fit and calibrate on your own labels.** Seconds, no gradient step, and the route is decided for you. Labels are a CSV with a `state` column and one column per question id; [`examples/data/routing_labels.csv`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/examples/data/routing_labels.csv) is a 60-row example that routes messages to billing, HR, PR, sales or technical and rates their urgency: ```csv state,team,urgency "We were charged twice for the March invoice, please refund the duplicate.",billing,2 "I would like to apply for the open backend engineer role. Where do I send my CV?",hr,0 "A journalist from the Economic Times is asking for a comment on today's outage.",pr,2 ``` The whole loop, from import to the answer, is [`examples/42_fit_and_calibrate_vegaml.py`](https://github.com/NandhaKishorM/laya/blob/main/examples/42_fit_and_calibrate_vegaml.py). It holds out 4 rows per team (20), fits on the other 40, and measures the same 20 rows before and after. Condensed: ```python import csv, laya questions = { "team": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which team should handle this message?", "criteria": {"billing": "invoices, payments, refunds", "hr": "jobs, payroll, leave, policy", "pr": "press, media, public statements", "sales": "pricing, demos, quotes, trials", "technical": "bugs, outages, API and product questions"}}, "urgency": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How soon does this need a reply?", "criteria": ["can wait", "this week", "today"]}, } rows = list(csv.DictReader(open("examples/data/routing_labels.csv"))) held, fit_rows = rows[-20:], rows[:-20] # the script holds out 4 per team; same idea agent = laya.Agent(vegaml=True) print(laya.VegaAgent.min_rows(questions)) # 35: the fewest rows fit() accepts for these questions before = agent.predict(held[0]["state"], questions)["answers"]["team"] # the cold engine report = agent.fit([{"state": r["state"], "gold": {"team": r["team"], "urgency": r["urgency"]}} for r in fit_rows], questions=questions) # or agent.fit("examples/data/routing_labels.csv", questions=questions) print(report["n_fit"], report["n_calibrate"]) # 30 fit the heads, 10 are held out inside fit() to calibrate on print(report["serving"]) # the questions whose head beat the engine on the same rows print(report["calibration"]["band"]) # the review line per question, or None where it could not hold after = agent.predict(held[0]["state"], questions)["answers"]["team"] agent.save_calibration("fit-routing/") # he
